corrected_value.title: Relation of promoter methylation of the structural oxytocin gene to critical life events in major depression: A case control study

decisions.quote: Recently, we found hypomethylation of OXT in patients with Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) compared to healthy controls (HC). Since the replicability of findings is a key point of criticism in (epi‑)genetic research, we aimed to confirm our previous findings in a pre-registered study (data was stored in a database prior to pre-registration) within a new sample of n = 85 patients with MDD and n = 85 HC.
decisions.location: Current primary Abstract; complete deposited references and independently verified original reports0121
decisions.reason: Apply Step2 description matching to the actual reported finding, not to hypothetical unseen analyses. The current85MDD/85HC abstract explicitly retests prior OXT hypomethylation in MDD versus healthy controls. Within its complete deposited references, the JAD2020case-control article at821has a primary-author abstract explicitly reporting this finding in90MDD/90HC. The other2020OXT article abstract reports146MDD inpatients and within-patient stress/severity/sex analyses, not the specified HC contrast;2021SLC6A4is a different gene. Thus only the JAD report positively fits the described empirical contrast under the available primary evidence. Select already shipped821by description. This does not claim that an inaccessible other body contains no secondary control analysis or that every2024finding is attributed; current in-text attribution remains unavailable. The final expert uncertainty rests on a merely possible hidden analysis rather than a second positively equally fitting reported finding and is explicitly superseded. No extra original or missing pair is created.
